acceptance_gate: Pair the same fresh tasks and starting examples, admit the same semantic hypothesis set in every arm, and charge source acquisition, fitting and all rejected and successful checks.
completion_gate: Return a program for each task, evaluate all inputs, compare first-consistent and common-order controls and replay all reported correctness and cost arithmetic.
objective: Fit the same fresh Boolean rules from identical labeled examples with and without a previously saved fold. Charge original acquisition, downstream setup, fitting and exact verification, and test whether reusable structure lowers the total work.
status: On 32 fresh read-once Boolean rules each arm returned 32 exact programs over all 768 inputs. Prioritizing the fold reduced checks from 136 to 129 but took 11.243 s including source acquisition, versus 0.101 s with primitives alone. The downstream times alone were 0.186 s and 0.101 s. A common semantic order required the same 102 checks in both arms.
stop_rule: Keep every proposal, counterexample and failure from the frozen panel and report the paired outcome at the observed workload.
title: Can a saved fold lower the work of learning a new rule?
